id.description: Identifier for correlating the response with the corresponding ping request

alerts.description: (optional) Enables alert notifications for all devices of a SmartHQ user. (Defaults to false if not specified.)

kind.description: Event delivery channel type (pubsub refers to the publish-subscribe messaging pattern used internally). When the communication channel is WebSockets, use "websocket#pubsub". When the communication channel is HTTPS / SNS Callbacks, use "user#pubsub"

action.description: Action for event configuration (pubsub used for internal routing). This parameter is only included in the WebSocket payload

services.description: (optional) Enables receiving device and service events to be sent for all devices of a SmartHQ user. (Defaults to false if not specified.)

presence.description: (optional) Enables online/offline status events for all devices of a SmartHQ user. (Defaults to false if not specified.)

pubsub.description: Enables events for the account (pubsub used for internal messaging). Also notifies when new devices are added. Must be set to true to receive device specific updates.

commands.description: (optional) Enables command-outcome events for all devices of a SmartHQ user. Outcomes are only sent to the application which issued the command. (Defaults to false if not specified.)

/.send.summary: SmartHQ sends event messages as they occur on devices in real time over the communication channel

/.receive.summary: SmartHQ receives event configuration messages that specify which types of events you want to be notified about

info.description:
The Event Stream API is an AsyncAPI specification that defines the messages exchanged between SmartHQ and your application for real-time device updates. For example, when a washing machine finishes its cycle, SmartHQ can immediately send an event payload so your application knows "wash complete" in real time.

 The following specification is written from the perspective of SmartHQ.

 - **Event Configuration Messages** SmartHQ receives messages from your application that set your preferences for what events SmartHQ should send as they occur—alerts, presence, device state changes, and command outcomes.

- **Event Messages** SmartHQ sends the resulting updates (events) to your application over the communication channel as they happen in real time. 

We currently support delivering these messages over **WebSocket** and **HTTPS/SNS callbacks**.

## More Documentation
 See our **[Real-Time Device Updates Guide](https://docs.smarthq.com/device-control-and-monitoring/real-time-device-updates/)** for further guidance and more information.

This API spec below is designed to be machine-readable; for a human-friendly overview that describes the message format, example messages, and message channels (WebSockets and HTTPS/SNS callbacks) see our [documentation](https://docs.smarthq.com/device-control-and-monitoring/real-time-device-updates/).
